messages:
maria: FYI — starting Apex LoRA bring-up. We merged their LoRA into base-release v2.3 and ran a tiny quick-eval with 4-bit quant. Not great: invoice amounts sometimes get truncated or rounded oddly. Sharing short logs and a couple example prompts.

sam: Thanks — can you paste the eval metrics? Is it token-prob shift or decoding artifact?

maria: Quick summary from the smoke pack:
- Perplexity delta (4bit vs fp16): +2.8
- Avg token logprob shift on numeric tokens: -0.9
- Exact match on invoice amount (in test set of 120): 86% -> 71%

Example prompt that regresses: 
```
Prompt: 
"Invoice: Total due $1,234.56. Please extract the amount."
FP16 -> "$1,234.56"
4-bit -> "$1,234"
```

tejas: Hmm. That smells like quantization amplifying rounding in the attention/softmax for number tokens. Did you try the per-head KV scaling patch (softmerge) we used on previous int4 cases?

maria: Not yet. I ran a baseline straight merge + awq 4bit config. Config snippet: 
```
quant: awq
bits: 4
block_size: 128
per_channel: true
```

sam: Can you repro locally with the reproducible eval script? Use the apex evalpack and --seed 42 to stabilize. Command: 
```
./scripts/run_quick_eval.sh --model merged/apex-lora-v2.3-awq4 --evalpack packs/apex-invoice-v1 --out out/apex-awq4.json --seed 42
```

ben: Customer impact: their parser expects exact cents to route payments. 71% exact will trigger support tickets. If softmerge helps, can we prioritize?

tejas: Two quick experiments to try in parallel: 
1) Softmerge with per-layer float residuals on the numeric head weights. (This dampens quant noise.)
2) Requant with block_size=32 and symmetric rounding. I expect (1) better for amounts.

sam: I'll spin up a small runner on my laptop to test both. If someone can drop the evalpack and a small sample subset in /tmp/apex-smoke, I can run both in <30m.

maria: Dropped subset (10 cases) to 
https://internal-storage.redwood/apex/smoke-subset-10.json
Also uploaded the merged model tar to 
https://s3.redwood/models/apex-lora-merged-v2.3-awq4.tar.gz

ci-bot: ci:quick-smoke started for apex-lora-merged-v2.3-awq4 (job 8347). Expect ~12m. :rocket:

sam: Ran both experiments locally: results (exact-match on subset of 10):
- baseline awq4: 7/10
- softmerge (per-layer float residuals on numeric heads): 9/10
- awq4 block32 symmetric: 8/10

Logs: 
```
Softmerge run: out/softmerge_apex.json
Metric: exact_amount = 0.9
Avg token logprob shift (numeric tokens) = -0.3
```

tejas: That aligns with hypothesis. Softmerge reduces the quant-induced bias. We should also check latency/throughput delta; softmerge keeps a small float patch so might add ~3-5% token latency.

maria: Can you drop the softmerge patch into a canary on dedicated for a day? If metrics look stable, we can recommend that quantization profile for Apex. Also we should add a regression test in the evalpack that checks exact_amount >= 0.88 for any future merges.

sam: On it. I'll prepare a canary config: 
```
model: apex-lora-v2.3
quant_profile: awq4-softmerge
canary: true
traffic: 0.5%
metrics: [exact_amount, token_latency, p95_latency]
```

ben: Heads up to customer success before canary goes live — they'll want an opt-in notification. I'll prepare the note.

maria: Great. Follow-ups:
- tejas: write brief doc on softmerge parameters we used (layer whitelist = ['decoder.layers.10','decoder.layers.11'], residual_scale=0.02)
- sam: run the canary and post telemetry after 6h
- ben: coordinate CS message

ci-bot: ci:quick-smoke (job 8347) passed all smoke tests.

maria: Thanks all — leaving this thread open for telemetry. If canary looks good by EOD I'll roll the quant profile into the customer merge guide. :thumbsup:
